gaps.lead: He couldn't swim until he was twenty.
gaps.sentence: He ___ swim until he was twenty.
gaps.explanation: couldn't = was not able to (general ability in the past).

gaps.lead: The results were announced, and immediately people began celebrating.
gaps.sentence: The results had ___ people began celebrating.
gaps.explanation: No sooner had the results been announced than people began…

gaps.lead: I regret not studying harder at university.
gaps.explanation: 'I regret not doing' = 'I wish I had done' — wish + past perfect for past regrets.

gaps.lead: Jogging every morning was completely normal for him.
gaps.explanation: be used to + -ing = be accustomed to.

gaps.lead: You can only get a seat if you book well in advance.
gaps.explanation: if you don't book = without booking.

gaps.lead: Brian was really interested in North American history in his school days.
gaps.sentence: Brian ___ North American history in his school days.
gaps.hint: be interested in = have an ___ in
gaps.explanation: 'To be interested in' becomes the noun pattern: 'had an interest in'.
